title: Claiming Our Rights: Feminist Discourses in Bangladesh and South Asia
description: A collection of essays Dr. Hossain wrote over several decades, following how the women's rights movement in Bangladesh and South Asia developed its arguments over almost fifty years. The essays look at women in policymaking, in markets and in parliament, and at how women organised politically.
notes: Hardcover, 321 pp (library records: xiii + 321). Pathak Shamabesh gives 'first published September 2023'. List price Tk 1,000. In November 2026 the UPL and Pathak Shamabesh pages said 'Not Available For Sale'; Rokomari still had a Buy button. No Google Books or WorldCat record was opened.

title: The Company Weavers of Bengal: The East India Company and the Organization of Textile Production in Bengal, 1750-1813
publisher: Oxford University Press, Delhi (Oxford University South Asian Studies Series), 1988; Bangladesh edition: The University Press Limited, Dhaka, 2010
description: A revised version of Dr. Hossain's Oxford DPhil thesis (1982). It uses newly found eighteenth-century Bengali records of the East India Company to argue that the Company's push for low wages and strict control over weavers helped bring down the Bengal weaving industry, and it describes the weavers' lives and working conditions.
notes: OUP 1988: xvii + 211 pp, 8 pp of plates. UPL 2010: xix + 211 pp. Both include a bibliography (pp. 195-203) and an index. No other reprints were found. In November 2026 the UPL page said 'Not Available For Sale'; Rokomari listed it at Tk 544.

title: Of the Nation Born: The Bangladesh Papers
authors: Hameeda Hossain and Amena Mohsin (eds); introduction by Meghna Guhathakurta
publisher: Zubaan, New Delhi (Zubaan Series on Sexual Violence and Impunity in South Asia); distributed by the University of Chicago Press
description: The Bangladesh volume of Zubaan's IDRC-supported series on sexual violence and impunity in South Asia. It brings together essays, interviews and case studies on sexual violence from the 1971 war onward, covering law, nationalism, memory, minorities and the feminist campaigns for recognition and accountability.
notes: The publisher's page (https://zubaanbooks.com/shop/of-the-nation-born/) exists but blocked automated access, so its content was not checked. Page counts differ: 320 pp (UChicago) and xlviii + 369 pp (a library record). Several retailers show it out of stock. A Bengali expanded edition was published separately (see ekti-jatir-janma).

title: Ekti Jatir Janma: Youn Shohingsota o Daymukti (একটি জাতির জন্ম: যৌন সহিংসতা ও দায়মুক্তি)
description: The Bengali translation and expanded edition of Of the Nation Born. Alongside the translated essays it adds interviews, case studies, and extracts from poems, novels and stories about sexual violence in 1971 and the impunity that followed.
notes: In Bengali. 426 pp (UPL) or 411 pp (Rokomari). Rokomari lists it as out of stock and UPL says 'Not Available For Sale'.

title: Freedom from Fear, Freedom from Want? Re-thinking Security in Bangladesh
authors: Hameeda Hossain, Meghna Guhathakurta and Malini Sur
publisher: Rupa & Co., New Delhi, for WISCOMP (Women in Security, Conflict Management and Peace); series: Revisioning and EnGendering Security: Gender and Non-Traditional Aspects of Security in South Asia
description: A short study of how state formation and political governance in Bangladesh create fear and insecurity for women by putting male experience at the centre. It treats both the state and globalising markets as sources of insecurity, especially for women from religious minorities, and uses the ideas of 'freedom from fear' and 'freedom from want' as its frame.
notes: 63 pp. The Western Sydney University record names Rupa and Co. (India), 2010, and the ISBN. The WISCOMP page confirms the series. 'New Delhi' as the place is inferred from Rupa's base. No retailer listing was found; this is probably out of print.

title: Human Rights in Bangladesh: Past, Present and Future
authors: Imtiaz Ahmed (ed.); 12 contributors including Hameeda Hossain
isbn: 9789845061520 (first edition); UPL also lists a second edition, ISBN 9789845064675
description: An edited volume of twelve essays and an introduction on human rights in Bangladesh, arranged in past, present and future sections. Dr. Hossain's Chapter 5, 'Human Rights in the Nation State' (in Part II, the present), argues that narrow readings of democracy, secularism and nationalism have drawn the state away from its founding ideals, and that powerful interests limit access to justice.
notes: The Daily Star review confirms Chapter 5, 'Human Rights in the Nation State', by Hameeda Hossain. A 2014 publication date fits the chapter's data running to May 2012. The UPL second-edition page also shows 2014 as first published and gives no year for the second edition. Both UPL pages said 'Not Available For Sale' in November 2026.

title: Rising from the Ashes: Women's Narratives of 1971
authors: Editorial board: Shaheen Akhtar, Suraiya Begum, Meghna Guhathakurta, Hameeda Hossain, Sultana Kamal; translated by Niaz Zaman; introduction by Mofidul Hoque; foreword by Hameeda Hossain
publisher: Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK) and The University Press Limited (UPL), Dhaka (Road to Bangladesh series)
description: The English translation of ASK's 2001 Bengali collection of oral histories, Narir Ekattor. It gathers the testimonies of 22 women who lived through killings, rape, eviction and displacement in 1971, and their later struggles for survival and justice.

links.label: Review, The Daily Star (A tale not often told)

notes: Dr. Hossain is also on the editorial board, and UPL and Rokomari list her as an editor. Her foreword is confirmed by The Daily Star review. Length: 298 pp (UPL) or 284 pp (Rokomari, 2nd impression). In November 2026 the UPL page said 'Not Available For Sale'; Rokomari listed it at Tk 560.

title: From Crisis to Development: Coping with Disasters in Bangladesh
authors: Hameeda Hossain, Cole P. Dodge and F. H. Abed (eds)
description: An edited volume written after the 1991 cyclone, on how Bangladesh copes with disasters and how relief can connect to longer-term development. It includes studies sponsored by UNICEF, BRAC and ICDDR,B.
notes: xviii + 398 pp, with illustrations and maps (library record). Rokomari lists it as out of stock.

title: No Better Option? Industrial Women Workers in Bangladesh
authors: Hameeda Hossain, Roushan Jahan and Salma Sobhan
description: An early study of women working in Bangladesh's industrial sector, written with Roushan Jahan and the lawyer Salma Sobhan. It examines why women took factory work and the conditions they faced.
notes: Open Library gives the authors, UPL, 1990 and 126 pp. A second record (Dec 1993, 200 pp) carries the ISBN 9840511327. The description is based on the title and subtitle only; no publisher or retailer page was found.

title: Gendered Lives, Livelihood and Transformation: The Bangladesh Context
description: An anthology of fieldwork-based studies of women's lives and work in Bangladesh as it moved from a subsistence economy to a capitalist one. Its subjects include indigenous women in jhum cultivation, Dalit women, female-headed rural households and elderly women in city slums.
notes: The bibliographic details are confirmed by the UPL page (2017, 198 pp) and Open Library. Dr. Hossain's chapter is reported only in a search summary of the LSE review, which says she and Suraiya Begum studied how the livelihoods of Munda and Rishi women in south-west Bangladesh are changing. The review PDF (researchonline.lse.ac.uk/id/eprint/88553) was downloaded but its text could not be extracted and the chapter title was not found. Note the title says 'Livelihood' (singular).

title: Human Rights in Bangladesh (Ain o Salish Kendra annual report series)
authors: Ain o Salish Kendra; edited by Hameeda Hossain for several years
publisher: Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK), Dhaka (earlier volumes with The University Press Limited)
isbn: Varies by volume, e.g. 9789843235992 (2005 volume, pub. 2006)
description: ASK's yearly review of the human rights situation in Bangladesh, covering law enforcement, violence against women, minorities, freedom of expression and access to justice. Dr. Hossain edited many volumes of the series in the 2000s.

links.label: Review of Human Rights in Bangladesh 2004, The Daily Star

notes: Confirmed from pages opened: 2000 (editor Dr. Hossain) and 2006 (Dr. Hossain with Sara Hossain) from the CiNii notes, and 2004 (ed. Dr. Hossain, ASK 2005, 244 pp) from The Daily Star. The 2002, 2005 (269 pp) and 2008 (xv + 266 pp) volumes were attributed to her only in search summaries of BRAC University library records, which could not be opened because of a bot check. The 2003 volume was edited by Dina M. Siddiqi, not Dr. Hossain. The 1997 and 1998 volumes (UPL) name no editor in the sources seen. The full list of years she edited is not confirmed.
